title: NumPy Array Indexing & Slicing Visualizer
description: Step-by-step visual trace of 1D and 2D indexing, row selection, column selection via the colon (:) operator, and sub-matrix slicing across rows and columns.

steps.explanation: Imports the NumPy numerical computing library under the conventional alias 'np'.
Allocates a contiguous 4x3 two-dimensional NumPy array storing marks for 4 students across 3 subjects (Maths, English, Science).
Evaluates marks[0]. In a 2D array, a single integer index selects the entire row at index 0 (Student 1's scores).
Evaluates marks[-1]. Negative indexing counts backwards from the end, cleanly accessing the final row (Student 4's scores) without needing to compute the length.
Evaluates marks[:, 0]. The colon (:) in row position selects all rows, while 0 selects Column 0, returning all Maths marks as a 1D vector.
Evaluates marks[1, 1]. In 2D coordinate indexing [row, column], this navigates to row index 1 (Student 2) and column index 1 (English), isolating the scalar value 85.
Evaluates marks[0:2, :]. Slices rows 0 through 1 (start 0 included, stop 2 excluded) and all columns (:), extracting a 2x3 sub-matrix for the first two students.
Evaluates marks[0:2, 2]. Combines row slicing (rows 0 and 1) with column indexing (column 2: Science), yielding a 1D array of Science marks for the first two students.
